newsitem.title: TAIWAN: ADB to issue $200-260m Taiwan-dollar bonds in Dec.
newsitem.headline: ADB to issue $200-260m Taiwan-dollar bonds in Dec.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank has applied to Taiwan's central bank to issue US$200-260 million in Taiwan-dollar-denominated bonds in early December, lead underwriter Chinatrust Bank said on Friday.
"ADB has selected Chinatrust Bank as lead underwriter for the bonds, but most deails have yet to be set," Chinatrust spokeswoman Wang Li said by telephone.
The bond issue will have a term of seven to 10 years, and the amount will be between US$200 million and $260 million, she said.
ADB originally had scheduled a June launch date for a 10-year, US$200 million issue, but it later postponed the issue without giving a reason.
The December issue would be ADB's second issue denominated in Taiwan dollars.
Taiwan's central bank had said ADB's planned bond issue would help internationalise Taiwan's bond market and raise the credibility of Taiwan's currency.
In August 1995, the ADB issued a seven-year Taiwan dollar-denominated bond valued at T$2.6 billion, or roughly US$100 million. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
